# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences a fast heart rate when playing, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, are reported in approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has bowel problems, which is his main current issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and subtle anomalies of the palate can affect speech development and feeding in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls down frequently, more than other kids his age, and has difficulty with speech, which may indicate neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay, seizures, and tethered cord are reported in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often asking "what" when spoken to, indicating potential hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Conductive hearing loss, glue ear, and recurrent otitis media are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems, seeing far-away things as too close, which may indicate myopia or other vision issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, such as astigmatism, myopia, and hypermetropia, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak tooth enamel, according to the dentist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel and large front teeth are common dental concerns in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty communicating effectively, which affects his education and daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need special education plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and falls frequently, indicating potential developmental and behavioral issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers, curved fingers, and spinal issues, are reported in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth enamel and overall dental health
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate potential heart issues
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess potential skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and communication difficulties
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring of bowel problems and adjustment of treatment as needed

Parent: Oh, yes... her eyesight isn't perfectly normal. She has astigmatism, which means she needs glasses to see clearly. It's been a challenge finding frames she likes and keeping them clean, but we're managing.

Parent: Sometimes I feel like I have to call her name several times before she responds. It's not that she can't hear me; it's more like she's just not paying attention or is too focused on what she's doing. I worry that maybe there's an underlying issue we should look into.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has been a bit of a problem for her. Harder foods like apples or meat are difficult for her to manage. We've had to adapt mealtime to include softer options or cut things into smaller pieces to make it easier for her.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, the heart. We have to go for regular check-ups to monitor everything. It's reassuring to know that the doctors are keeping a close eye on her condition. I just wish there was more we could do to prevent any future issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Coordination seems to be a bit of an issue. When she runs or tries to do complex movements, she appears less steady than her peers. I'm worried it might affect her confidence or ability to participate in certain activities.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Mealtime can be stressful. She has trouble eating certain textures or foods and often leaves meals unfinished. We've tried various strategies to make mealtime more enjoyable and stress-free.

Parent: She has scoliosis, which affects her back. We're working closely with physical therapists to help improve her posture and reduce the risk of further complications. It's a lot to take in, but we're trying our best to support her through all these challenges.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has to go for regular check-ups to monitor heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble eating certain textures or foods, often leaving meals unfinished, and has difficulty with harder foods like apples or meat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, appearing less steady than her peers when running or doing complex movements, and has scoliosis affecting her back.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond immediately to her name, suggesting possible hearing or attention issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, requiring glasses to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects her back, and has coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups
* Regular hearing reviews
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Check position of testes in boys
* Consider a palate review
* Referral for a cardiac review
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull)
* Monitor growth velocity
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue more quickly than other kids his age, even during simple games, indicating potential respiratory or cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other kids his age, suggesting possible cardiac issues that may lead to fatigue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky about food and will often refuse to eat certain things, not just based on taste but also on preparation, indicating potential feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, taking longer to reach milestones such as walking and sitting up, and has speech delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with fluid in his ears, affecting his balance, and squints when trying to focus, indicating potential vision and hearing problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many have required multiple grommet insertions.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that the cardiologist monitors through regular appointments to assess its impact on her overall health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties during mealtimes, getting frustrated when eating, which affects her mood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a lack of interest in feeding being a significant and long-lasting issue in some cases.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears less coordinated compared to peers, with simple tasks requiring balance and movement seeming to challenge her more.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, seeming preoccupied or distracted, and has required more frequent dental check-ups and cleanings to prevent problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids, and some having speech delay linked to hearing concerns.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus, with her eyes seeming to get tired easily, and she has trouble seeing clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require more attention than usual, with the dentist recommending more frequent check-ups and cleanings to prevent problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel, making careful brushing important, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans due to the extra demands of mainstream secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to express herself in a way that others understand, leading to frustration during interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably shorter fingers than usual.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to prevent teeth problems
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movement struggles and has accidents often, which can be upsetting for both the patient and the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak muscles, diagnosed as hypotonia, which affects muscle tone.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing, particularly when called from a distance, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems, including crossed eyes and trouble seeing things far away, diagnosed as hypermetropia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods due to dental concerns, and has weak enamel.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is experiencing speech delays, taking longer to start talking than other kids of the same age.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental concerns and prevent complications.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss and speech delays.
* Eyesight review to correct vision problems and prevent further complications.
* Cardiac review to monitor heart structure and function.
* Referral for a skeletal review to assess spinal and hip development.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and muscle tone concerns.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular check-ups and monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, managed through diet and lifestyle adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring off into space and being unresponsive for a few seconds, which are being investigated by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV very high, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient reports blurry vision, especially when trying to read or watch TV from a distance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, which is a concern for potential cavities and dental problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience a variety of dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, which affects mobility and balance, but is managed with physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor weak enamel and prevent dental problems.
* Regular hearing reviews to assess and address potential hearing issues.
* Eyesight review to evaluate and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the pre-existing heart condition.
* Neurological evaluation to investigate and manage episodes of staring off into space.
* Physical therapy to improve mobility and balance affected by hip dysplasia.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient breathes more rapidly during intense play sessions than what's typically expected for a child her age, and there are concerns about potential heart issues that require monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky about food textures, which makes her uncomfortable or causes her to refuse meals altogether.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily, even with moderate exercise, and has developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have difficulties with neurological development.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated in very noisy environments and has trouble filtering out background noises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs her eyes when trying to focus on something, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than her peers, with potential orthodontic issues due to the size and spacing of these teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth, and may experience weak enamel and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may have difficulties with focus and attention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that require ongoing monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers, curved fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth size and spacing
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality in his heart that requires periodic monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits feeding aversion and has specific food refusals, making mealtime management stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord diagnosed after birth and exhibits developmental differences compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for repetitions, indicating potential hearing issues or difficulty processing auditory information.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, causing trouble focusing on objects at certain distances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem prone to breaking or chipping easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental differences compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and slightly different movements compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor astigmatism and other vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart valve abnormality.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor hip dysplasia and other skeletal issues.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental differences and feeding aversion.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality of the heart, which is being monitored closely with regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation and has trouble going to the bathroom regularly, requiring different diets and remedies to help her go more smoothly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, and a small number may require longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and experiences seizures, which are managed with medication and lifestyle changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, seeming to hear some sounds but not others clearly, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, squints, and leans forward to try and get a better look, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods due to potential dental concerns, and may require regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties are affecting her learning, and she may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems developmentally behind other children her age, requiring support from therapists and educators.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences, and may have autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal health.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental needs.
* Regular check-ups to monitor epilepsy and adjust medication as needed.
* Consider a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires management and monitoring by a cardiologist to prevent significant impact on daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion and is particular about what he eats, making meal times challenging, and there are also palatal abnormalities that are being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding, and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and is being monitored and treated by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often asking people to repeat themselves because he can't quite catch what they're saying the first time around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, especially when the teacher writes in small letters or from a distance, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist frequently due to various tooth issues, including cavities, and requires regular monitoring and treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups. Large front teeth are also common, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, though some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers. A small number of children have had hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and treat tooth issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and treat vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor and manage heart abnormalities.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal abnormalities.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support the patient's development and well-being.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of the valves in his heart, which is monitored regularly through check-ups with his cardiologist. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed through dietary changes and increased fluid intake.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more easily than his peers during physical activities, suggesting a possible neurological aspect, though no definitive diagnosis has been made yet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear last year, which caused temporary discomfort and affected his hearing. He also has palatal abnormalities that his doctors are monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs his eyes when trying to focus, especially when reading or watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weaker than average tooth enamel, making his teeth more susceptible to decay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves slightly differently compared to his peers, which is being explored further to understand its implications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has some skeletal issues, including possible implications of his movement differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth enamel and prevent decay
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental needs

a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the TV volume way up to hear properly, indicating potential hearing concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, which can make reading and writing a challenge.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily, which may indicate a heart condition. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has bowel problems and goes to the toilet many times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints a lot.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia of upper central incisors) and may have weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and some have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent any potential issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess the patient's vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to assess the patient's heart condition and address any concerns.
* Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor the patient's bone development and address any concerns.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioral differences.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Yes, we've noticed he sits very close to the TV or books. It's almost as if he can't see things clearly unless they're right in front of him. This has been going on for a while now, and we're getting a bit worried it might affect his eyesight in the long run.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Actually, yes. He always turns the volume of the TV very high. We're not sure if it's because he can't hear well or if he just likes it loud, but it's definitely something we've observed regularly. Sometimes we have to ask him to turn it down because it gets too loud for us.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth break or chip easily. We have to be really careful when he's eating or playing to make sure he doesn't hurt them. It's not just the front ones either; even the back teeth seem more prone to chipping than they should be at his age.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: He can't keep up with physical activity for long. If we're out playing or at the park, he gets tired much quicker than the other kids. We thought maybe he was just not into sports or running around, but it's happened often enough that we're starting to think there might be something more going on.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, he's been slower to reach some milestones. Like when he was learning to walk or sit up - it took him longer than our friends' kids. We're trying not to compare too much, but it's hard not to notice these differences.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He's often refused to eat certain foods. It's not just being picky; sometimes he'll even throw up if we try to get him to eat something new. We're managing okay for now by just sticking to what he likes‚ but we worry about him missing out on nutrients.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Generally‚ he seems behind other children in development. And specifically‚ we've noticed a speech delay. His vocabulary isn't as large as other kids his age‚ and forming sentences is still something he's working on. These are things we're keeping an eye on and discussing with his teachers and therapists.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, as evidenced by turning the TV volume up high and potential conductive hearing loss.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Honestly, I'm not entirely sure if it's a problem or just a habit, but my son tends to sit very close to the TV or when reading books. It's almost as if he can't see things clearly unless they're right in front of him.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: I've noticed that sometimes he seems to hear certain sounds just fine, but then there are other times when he doesn't seem to pick up on everything being said. It's confusing because it's not consistent - sometimes he hears me perfectly, and other times it's like he's not listening at all.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing can be a bit of a challenge for him. He has trouble with harder foods - like apples or meat. Soft foods are okay, but anything that requires a lot of chewing effort seems to be difficult.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... the doctors have mentioned a septal defect. I'm still trying to understand what that fully means and how it will affect him long-term, but essentially, there's an issue with the way his heart is structured.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He experiences epileptic seizures. We're working closely with his neurologist to manage them and find the best treatment plan. It's been a learning curve for us as parents to recognize the signs and know how to respond.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He has a feeding aversion to certain textures and tastes. It makes mealtime challenging because he's very particular about what he'll eat. 

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: My son was born with shorter fingers than typical, which has presented its own set of challenges. Additionally, he takes a bit longer to reach developmental milestones than we expected. We're monitoring his progress closely and working with therapists to support his development.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion to certain textures and tastes, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures and has a neurological condition that requires management and treatment.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has inconsistent hearing, with some sounds being heard clearly and others not, and may have conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the TV or when reading books, suggesting possible vision problems.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in his heart, which is being monitored by a cardiologist to ensure he receives the best care possible.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky with food textures, making mealtime challenging, and requires carefully prepared meals to avoid difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord that is being monitored by a neurologist for its progression and impact on development. He also has speech development concerns, as he is not speaking as much as expected for his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's hearing seems okay, but he often asks for things to be repeated to understand them better.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's eyes get rubbed a lot, especially when trying to focus, and there are concerns about potential long-term effects on his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental problems due to his teeth structure, making him more susceptible to cavities and other issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development is a concern, and he may require additional support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech development concerns and may require additional support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer to close than usual, and he has a tethered cord.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curved fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental problems
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Neurological monitoring to track the progression of the tethered cord and its impact on development
* Speech therapy to support speech development
* Occupational therapy to support fine motor skills and feeding difficulties
* Behavioural therapy to support behavioural differences and anxiety
* Regular monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be very particular about food textures and may refuse to try certain foods due to their texture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires quickly during playtime or running around, similar to her heart issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the TV volume up really high, but hearing tests have shown no issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her ability to see clearly, but is managed with glasses and regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require a lot of maintenance, with frequent dentist visits to ensure they stay healthy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia and also has scoliosis, requiring mindful mobility and preventive measures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of her heart valves, requiring regular check-ups with a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, having trouble passing stools regularly and often complains of feeling bloated or uncomfortable after meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination challenges, appearing less steady on her feet compared to her peers, especially in certain situations like running or engaging in sports.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is easily overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated in crowded or noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs her eyes, especially when trying to focus, and seems to strain to see clearly, particularly during screen time or reading.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than her peers, affecting her smile and bite, and requires close monitoring and good oral hygiene practices.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to lag behind her peers developmentally, with certain skills and milestones taking longer to achieve than expected, prompting discussions about possible interventions or support systems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and may benefit from interventions or support systems to address these gaps.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and may experience hip dysplasia or scoliosis.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and oral hygiene.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially given the patient's sensitivity to noise.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to address any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support the patient's developmental and behavioural needs.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition involving a valve that requires regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient does not gain weight like other kids and has feeding difficulties, although he eats okay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient trips over his own feet sometimes, has difficulty with sports, and has scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media and complains of blurry vision, which may be related to his eyes or ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth pain when eating cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient does not talk as much as he should for his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may have difficulties with speech and social interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and may have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth pain and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for scoliosis and other skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's developmental delays and behavioural differences.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has abnormal heart valves.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion and difficulty eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems less coordinated when moving and has difficulty making himself understood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in his ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and dental concerns, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty making himself understood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Consider referral for a skeletal review to monitor spinal and hip health
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and coordination
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Honestly, I've noticed he often squints when looking at things. It's like he's having trouble focusing or something. I'm not sure what's going on, but it seems to bother him.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yeah... noisy places really get to him. He gets frustrated easily when there's too much noise around. I try to keep an eye on him in those situations.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teech... they break or chip easily. We have to be super careful what he eats and make sure he brushes them regularly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The doctors said he needs regular heart check-ups. That's all I know about it so far. They just said it's something they want to monitor.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has seziures. It's scary when it happens because we never know when it will occur. The doctors are helping us manage it though.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been a challenge. He has difficulties with eating certain foods and sometimes throws up. We're working on finding the right balance for him.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Well... he takes a bit longer to reach some milestones than we expected. And he moves a bit differently compared to his peers. Like, his walking and running style is not entirely like other kids his age. But we love him just the way he is!
